findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. They can describe the project after reading only this paragraph.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: Someone arriving at Athena's own site finds a title about a different project, firstmate. The second and third paragraphs explain that the page is a study made as a demonstration, but the title and nearly everything after the header are about firstmate rather than Athena.
findings.source: Title / h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The pitch rests on tracing each result to its models, cost and verdict, but the page never shows those for its own study. A newcomer sees no model names, cost or checker verdict, so the main selling point is described but not shown.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The next steps are concrete and in order: what you need first, how to clone, how to install, and a first command to try. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link appears in the header right after the newcomer's next step, but it is for the project owner. A first-time visitor has no proposals waiting and may not know whether the link applies to them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision

findings.text: The Counters section names transitions by id before the Transitions section defines them. For a reader new to firstmate, the middle of the page is dense, though the glossary and the "Words used first" list help.
findings.source: Counters: "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact lines at a pinned commit. A newcomer can check the page's own promise of traceability.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: The page says plainly that nothing was run and every claim comes from reading the code. This helps a newcomer judge how far to trust it.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"

findings.text: This closing section points to an internal folder without saying where it lives. A newcomer gets no use from it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
